references.text: The preceding context describing the situation where an Israelite sells himself to a foreigner, and the possibilities for redemption by relatives.
The continuation explaining how the redemption price is calculated based on the number of years remaining until the Jubilee year.
The fundamental law concerning the Jubilee year (שְׁנַת הַיֹּבֵל), which is central to calculating the redemption price in verse 50.
The principle that an Israelite servant should be treated as a hired worker (שָׂכִיר), using the same term found in verse 50.
Reiterating the principle that the servant shall be like a hired worker (כִּשְׂכִיר שָׁנָה בְּשָׁנָה), corresponding to the expression in verse 50.
The comparison of a bondservant's service with the value of a hired worker's wages, the same concept as in Leviticus 25:50.
Reference to the years of a hired worker (כִּשְׁנֵי שָׂכִיר) as a measure of time, using language similar to that in verse 50.
Job compares human life to the days of a hired worker (כִּימֵי שָׂכִיר), the same expression used in Leviticus 25:50.
